$comment: C16 GOVERNED CLOSURE EXCLUSIONS — fail-closed by construction.
This file is NOT how platform-incompatible packages are removed. Those are
dropped by the closure engine from each package's OWN recorded os/cpu/libc
conditions in pnpm-lock.yaml, and every drop is reported as evidence.
This file exists only for an exclusion a human must justify. Every entry must
bind ALL of: target, scope, the FULL resolution key (name@version with peer
suffix), the parent edge it hangs from, a reason, evidence, an owner, and a
* wildcards or name-only entries (no version / no resolution key)
* an entry whose resolution key is absent from the lock-derived closure (stale)
* an entry that never actually suppressed anything during the run (unused)
* an entry whose recorded version no longer matches the lock (changed version)
* an exclusion of a MANDATORY dependency that is target-compatible
The list is intentionally EMPTY: nothing in the current closure requires a
human-justified exclusion. An empty list is the honest state, and the reconciler
still runs every rejection rule against it.
